subject: Starter reserve pool & ramp options — clarifying structure and billing cadence
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@sproutai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Diaz <marco@sproutai.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Starter prepay / reserve pool question

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited about Redwood's latency profile and the cost tools you showed. We're a small infra team and trying to decide between a straight monthly plan or a 12–18 month prepay to get predictable unit economics during our series A growth. A couple quick questions so we can model this: 

- Are there starter-level prepay structures with a pooled "reserve" of credits we can use for burst capacity (e.g., for launch weekends) that vest over the term?
- Typical term discounts for early-stage customers at 12 months vs 18 months?
- Can we have a cap on overage rate and quarterly invoices (we prefer fewer invoices to keep AP overhead low)?

Attached is a short RFP summary so you have context on our usage patterns.

[Attachment: SproutAI_RFP_Summary.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Elena Morales
Head of Infrastructure, SproutAI
elena@sproutai.com

P.S. Marco's included to help with procurement questions.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@sproutai.com>
Cc: Marco Diaz <marco@sproutai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Starter prepay / reserve pool question

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the RFP. Short answers up front, then a couple starter structures we commonly propose for teams at your stage.

Quick answers:
- Yes: we can create a reserve pool (prepaid credits) that vests monthly and is usable for burst capacity; unused credits roll forward but typically are consumed for any overages first.
- Term discounts: typical 12-month starter term is ~10–18% off list; 18–24 month terms often qualify for an additional 3–7% depending on committed spend.
- Overage caps and quarterly invoicing: yes, we can cap overage uplift (we usually do list+20% for guaranteed cap) and issue invoices quarterly against the prepaid balance.

Examples (illustrative):
Option A — 12-month starter prepay
- Prepay $60k up front (applied over 12 months)
- 15% term discount vs monthly list pricing
- Reserve pool: 40k token credits that vest 1/12 each month
- Quarterly invoicing (drawdown from prepaid pool)
- Overage cap at list+25%

Option B — 18-month ramped prepay
- Prepay $90k up front
- 18% term discount
- Reserve pool: 80k credits, vests monthly with a 3-month minimum consumption guarantee
- Quarterly invoices
- Overage cap at list+20%

If you want tighter commercial protections we can add a monthly minimum that steps up (ramped minimums) so both sides have predictability. If you can share an expected monthly baseline and peak multiplier for launch events, I can produce a tailored proposal with exact numbers.

Next steps: if any of the above looks close, I can draft a short-term LOI and get a draft MSA + payment schedule for procurement review. I cc'd Lauren for pricing flexibility — she can flag any startup-friendly concessions.

—Ben

Ben / team — quick internal note to shape the ask for procurement:

- If SproutAI is A-round and trajectory looks strong, I'm comfortable going to 18% on a 12-month package for a first-year pilot (conditional on a simple NRR/usage clause).
- Approve reserve pool mechanics as Ben described, but require a 6-month lookback to convert unused credits into account credits (avoid indefinite float).
- For AP, quarterly invoicing is fine. Finance wants banking details confirmed before DocuSign.

Ben: please include a clause that overage notifications run at 80% and 95% consumption so they get warnings before hitting the cap.

—Lauren

Subject: Re: Starter prepay / reserve pool question

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few clarifying asks from procurement and finance: 

- Can we get the 12-month option with the 18% discount you mentioned as "startup-friendly"? That's our preference; cash flow is tight but predictable.
- We need a quarterly invoice schedule with Net 30 payment terms and one consolidated invoice per quarter (drawn against the prepaid balance).
- For the reserve pool, can the vesting be front-loaded slightly (first two months 20% vest, then even monthly vesting afterwards) — helps with launch prep.
- Can you provide a DocuSign-ready MSA and a PO-ready quote so we can pull approvals?

I've attached a lightly redlined MSA to highlight legal concerns.

[Attachment: Draft_MSA_v2_redlined.docx (Word)]

If you can send a DocuSign link and a one-page summary of the commercial terms we can get procurement moving this week.

Best,
Elena

Elena / Marco — great to align. Summary of agreed commercial terms below (we'll convert into a DocuSign package + PO-ready quote):

Summary — SproutAI starter prepay (agreed scope)
- Term: 12 months starting on mutually signed effective date
- Prepay: $60,000 up front (applied over term)
- Discount: 18% off list for the 12-month term
- Reserve pool: 50k token credits; vesting: 20% at month 1, 20% at month 2, then remaining 60% equally over months 3–12
- Invoicing: quarterly consolidated invoice, Net 30
- Overage: capped at list+25%; advanced notifications at 80% and 95% consumption
- Credit roll-forward: unused credits convert to account credit with 6-month lookback; exceptions to be handled case-by-case

Action items
1) Ben: prepare DocuSign package (MSA + quote) and upload to the HubSpot deal. Target: 48 hours.
2) Marissa (CC'd): please confirm finance wiring instructions and whether we can accommodate quarterly consolidated invoices for this new product flow.
3) Elena: if the summary looks right, please confirm and we'll issue DocuSign for signatures.
